To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combination of tegafur/uracil (FT-207, UFT) and leucovorin (LV) is an effective treatment for patients with advanced colorectal cancer (CRC).

(1) the addition of 5‐FU to tegafur‐uracil‐leucovorin (UFT‐LV) significantly improves the response rate of patients with advanced colorectal cancer (ORR 50 vs 26%, P = 0.0002), (2) 5‐FU‐UFT‐LV is well tolerated and (3) the addition of oxaliplatin to 5‐FU–UFT‐LV improves the response rate

the use of oral tegafuran and folinic acid as an alternative regimen for metastatic breast cancer is feasible and effective in patients who had previously been treated with anthracyclines and taxanes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the synthesis, the characterization and the biological evaluation of some new heterocyclic derivatives containing 1,2,4‐oxadiazole, 1,2‐oxazole and 1,3,4‐oxa‐diazole moieties as potential antimicrobials.
the synthesis and characterization of a new class of 5‐substituted 2‐(1H‐tetrazol‐5‐yl)‐1‐methyl‐1H‐imidazole‐4‐carboxamides (1a‐j), as well as their antimicrobial, cytotoxic and anti‐HIV activity.
the development of an oral regimen of tegafurs and folinic acid, in combination with a new formulation of calcium folinate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the combination of tegafur/uracil/leucovorin is not recommended for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who are not suitable for standard therapy.
the addition of folinic calcium to tegafur in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer is not recommended.
the use of oral tegafurs in the treatment of breast cancer is not yet established and should be considered investigational.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this is a well conducted study that provides evidence that the combination of tegafur/uracil and folinic acid can be used to treat patients with advanced breast cancer who have failed anthracyclines and taxanes.
it is not necessary to have a complete understanding of the mechanisms of a drug in order to use it in a safe and effective manner.
the combination of tegafur plus folinic acid has a modest activity in patients with previously untreated advanced breast cancer, with an acceptable toxicity profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a more comprehensive understanding of the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the development of resistance to 5‐FU and other drugs used to treat breast cancer.
we have shown that the combination of 5‐FU, folinic acid, and tegafur is an effective treatment for patients with metastatic breast cancer.
the addition of folinic Acid to tegafur can be an option to treat breast cancer.
